notes: Run evals/files/build-fixtures.sh <dir> first; the prompts below refer to <dir>/<fixture>. Fixture 1 mirrors a real rejected submission (careful code, approval-only AI session), so its expected verdict has ground truth.

evals.name: code-take-home-approval-only-transcript
evals.prompt: I've finished the Sniffspot promo-codes take-home and I'm about to push it. The repo is at <FIXTURES>/promo-codes-submission (the Lens from before is in docs/evaluator-expectations/). Can you check it against what the evaluators will be looking for before I send it? I'm applying for the backend role.
evals.expected_output: A full audit in one file, docs/submission-audit/audit.md, with verdict not-ready. Veto (AI direction) rated Missing: PROMPTS.md header is an echo ('very helpful', 'changed direction once on naming') and the transcript is 8/10 short approvals with every design choice proposed by the AI. First pass on SUBMISSION.md: decisions are facts without alternatives, no obstacle note, time 'about 3 hours'. Required events: 'AI got something wrong' Thin (wrong column name, no turn), 'changed direction' Thin (naming only), 'Decisions' Thin (4 entries, no alternatives), 'didn't get to' Thin. Code quality acknowledged (race-safe usage limit, case-insensitive index, snapshot) and weighted as tiebreaker; over-delivery flagged (max_uses was never asked for). Obstacle: not mentioned → Missing. Gaps ranked with veto first, marked make-it-happen-then-record (push back on the next proposals / disclose), not 'add'. Simulated final verdict close to the real rejection.
expectations: Writes exactly one output file, docs/submission-audit/audit.md (no audit-final.md, gaps.md, evidence.md, inventory.md or audit-partial.md), with kind: evaluator-audit, mode, verdict and ai_disclosure in its front-matter and the numbered sections Verdict, Scorecard, Deal breakers, Requirements, Submission package, AI disclosure, Deal makers, Gaps and fixes, Notes, and the Appendix
Verdict is not-ready, and the stated reason includes the veto criterion (AI direction) being Weak or Missing
First-pass verdict is written from SUBMISSION.md alone and notes at least two of: decisions without alternatives, no obstacle note, vague time
AI-direction evidence is rated Missing or Weak with the PROMPTS.md header identified as an echo/claim without turn references, and the transcript's approval-only pattern cited with a count or ratio
Required-to-exist events table rates 'moments where the AI got something wrong' and 'places where you changed direction' as Thin or Empty, citing that the only direction change is on naming
Planted obstacle is rated Missing or not-reported (no commit or note mentions anything broken in the existing codebase)
The race-safe usage limit is acknowledged as good engineering AND explicitly weighted as tiebreaker or flagged as over-delivery (max_uses was not in the brief)
Every Strong or Adequate rating in the scorecard has a file/section/commit/turn address

The Gaps and fixes section (§8) ranks the veto gap above every criterion and event gap (only blocks-review mechanics may precede it) and marks its retrofit as make-it-happen-then-record or disclose, not plain 'add'
The final simulated verdict in the evaluator's voice says the AI drove / the candidate approved, and the report notes it matches the Lens's 'current approach' prediction
The Appendix records the reading order (SUBMISSION.md first) and marks the video link as unverified, and the 6-commit range with timestamps is cited as evidence where it matters
The report does not invent criteria absent from the Lens (e.g. does not grade test coverage as a primary criterion)
The audit flags that docs/evaluator-expectations/ (the Lens) is tracked in the repo's history as a blocks-review finding with a fix that removes it from history before pushing
Every cited address (line number, commit hash, turn number) in audit.md can be verified against the submission; the grader found no fabricated citation

The AI disclosure section compares the PROMPTS.md claims with the transcript and rates the fit as contradicted or mismatch (the header claims direction changes the transcript does not show), with a fix that states the real share honestly rather than a lower number, and does not double-count AI direction already graded in the scorecard

The Requirements section lists unmet and partial requirements as full rows with their Lens IDs (E#/I#), severity, evidence reference and Lens reference, lists met ones by ID only, and every Critical requirement that is not met is reflected in the verdict's Why line or the must-do gaps

Every scorecard, trap, requirement, package and event row carries both an evidence reference into the submission (file and section or lines, commit, turn, message paragraph) or an explicit absence, and a Lens reference; every gap names the finding IDs it comes from

evals.name: text-proposal-fails-gate-and-veto
evals.prompt: here's my draft proposal for that shopify dashboard job (<FIXTURES>/dashboard-proposal/proposal.md, lens is in docs/evaluator-expectations). is it good enough to send? be honest
evals.expected_output: Full audit, verdict not-ready. Gate failed: the proposal does not start with a fitness product name (starts 'Hi there!'). Veto (post-launch trust) Missing: nothing about what happens when Shopify changes or after launch, no cadence, no support window. Other findings: opens with credentials not the client's problem; lists frameworks despite 'don't send me a list of frameworks'; 'show me' Shopify integration answered with generic portfolio links not a specific case; access list absent; timeline '2 weeks' with no buffer; no recurring costs. gaps.md gives the exact first line to add and the exact post-launch paragraph. First-pass verdict: closed after the first line.
expectations: Verdict is not-ready
Identifies the attention-filter gate as failed: the first words are a greeting, not a fitness product name
First-pass verdict states the client stops at the first line or paragraph
Veto (post-launch durability + reachability) rated Missing with the observation that the proposal says nothing about after launch, platform changes, cadence or a support window
Flags the framework/stack list as a tripped trap citing the brief's 'don't send me a list of frameworks'
Flags that the opening paragraph is about the submitter's credentials rather than the client's problem
Rates the Shopify 'show me' requirement as Weak: generic portfolio links, no specific named Shopify case

The Gaps and fixes section's first fix gives a literal first line (a home-fitness product name before any greeting) and a later fix gives quotable post-launch text (mechanism + cadence + bounded window)
Notes the missing 'what I'd need from you' access list as a required-to-exist event that is Empty
Does not credit the technical stack choice as a strength beyond one clause

Writes exactly one output file, docs/submission-audit/audit.md (no audit-final.md, gaps.md, evidence.md, inventory.md or audit-partial.md), with kind: evaluator-audit, mode, verdict and ai_disclosure in its front-matter and the numbered sections Verdict, Scorecard, Deal breakers, Requirements, Submission package, AI disclosure, Deal makers, Gaps and fixes, Notes, and the Appendix
The Submission package section covers each package item from the Lens (proposal, specific Shopify sample, access list) as present, thin or absent
The AI disclosure section is n-a or absent with low weight, since the client brief is silent on AI, and does not invent an AI criterion

Every scorecard, trap, requirement, package and event row carries both an evidence reference into the submission (file and section or lines, commit, turn, message paragraph) or an explicit absence, and a Lens reference; every gap names the finding IDs it comes from

evals.name: document-plus-spreadsheet-grant-application
evals.prompt: Can you audit my fellowship application before I submit? Everything's in <FIXTURES>/fellowship-application — narrative.md, budget.xlsx, work-sample.md — and the evaluator lens is in docs/evaluator-expectations. Deadline is next week so tell me what actually needs fixing.
evals.expected_output: Full audit, verdict not-ready. Gate: narrative exceeds the 1,500-word limit (measured ~1,667). Veto (community ownership vs product) Missing: the narrative opens with the platform, the community appears as 'pilot users', the question is 'question-agnostic', and the swap test fails. Handover (30%) Weak: 'publish a report and open-source the code' is exactly the non-plan the call names; no named custodian. Budget: tools total $9,000 = 22.5% > 15% ceiling, computed from the xlsx; amounts stored as text and total hardcoded flagged. Work sample: no two-sentence role split (applicant/community roles), and it's a client deliverable not a with-community piece. Relationship (30%): 'two paid workshops for the council' is not a relationship with the community. Learning section Adequate. Headings do not mirror the call's five points. Gaps: top one is make-it-happen (anchor on a real community) or disclose/don't apply.
expectations: Verdict is not-ready
Measures the narrative word count and reports it exceeds the 1,500-word limit as a gate failure, with the measured number
Veto (community ownership) rated Missing, citing that the narrative opens with the platform and the community appears as pilot users / the question is question-agnostic
Handover plan rated Weak or Missing, explicitly noting that 'publish a report' / 'open-source the code' is the non-plan the call itself rejects and that no named custodian exists
Opens budget.xlsx and computes tools/equipment as a share of the total (about 22-23%) against the 15% ceiling, reporting it as a finding
Flags at least one spreadsheet hygiene issue (amounts stored as text, or hardcoded total instead of a formula)
Work sample rated Weak or Missing on the required two-sentence role split (applicant's role vs community's role)
Relationship criterion (30%) rated Weak or Missing, noting that paid council workshops are not a relationship with the named community
Notes that narrative headings do not map to the call's five numbered points and that section lengths are not proportional to the published weights
Top gap is marked make-it-happen-then-record or disclose (a real community relationship cannot be written in), with the honest alternative of not applying this cycle stated
Scorecard uses the published weights (30/20/30/20) from the Lens and every Adequate-or-better rating has an address

Writes exactly one output file, docs/submission-audit/audit.md (no audit-final.md, gaps.md, evidence.md, inventory.md or audit-partial.md), with kind: evaluator-audit, mode, verdict and ai_disclosure in its front-matter and the numbered sections Verdict, Scorecard, Deal breakers, Requirements, Submission package, AI disclosure, Deal makers, Gaps and fixes, Notes, and the Appendix

The Requirements section lists unmet and partial requirements as full rows with their Lens IDs (E#/I#), severity, evidence reference and Lens reference, lists met ones by ID only, and every Critical requirement that is not met is reflected in the verdict's Why line or the must-do gaps

Every scorecard, trap, requirement, package and event row carries both an evidence reference into the submission (file and section or lines, commit, turn, message paragraph) or an explicit absence, and a Lens reference; every gap names the finding IDs it comes from

evals.name: partial-mode-halfway-checkpoint
evals.prompt: I'm about 2 hours into the 4-hour rate limiter exercise. Repo is at <FIXTURES>/rate-limiter-halfway, lens in docs/evaluator-expectations. Quick checkpoint — am I on track, what haven't I done yet that they'll be looking for?
evals.expected_output: Partial mode only: writes docs/submission-audit/audit.md with mode: partial, no verdict, no score. Events table: DESIGN.md algorithm section Present; race handling Present (Lua script, guarantees and non-guarantees stated); Redis-down decision Not yet; clock-skew analysis Not yet (though code uses Redis TIME — note it's a one-line write-up away); RESULTS.md raw output Not yet (no load test exists); interpretation paragraph Not yet; 'what you'd do with another 4 hours' Not yet; README clean-checkout run path Not yet (WIP stub). Veto proof (a load test that can fail) not visible yet. Do-next: build the load test harness now (multi-process, separate connections, one hot key, ≥60s) because it is the veto and takes the longest; then the two DESIGN sections; README last. Flags that the load test is the thing most at risk of never happening in the remaining 2 hours.
expectations: Runs in partial mode: writes docs/submission-audit/audit.md with mode: partial in its front-matter, writes no other output file, and does NOT assign a ship/fix-first/not-ready verdict or a weighted score
Events table marks the DESIGN.md algorithm and race-handling sections as Present/happened with addresses
Events table marks Redis-down decision, clock-skew analysis, RESULTS.md raw output, the interpretation paragraph, and 'another 4 hours' as not yet
States that the veto proof (a load test that could catch an over-admission) does not exist yet

The do-next list makes building the load-test harness the first substantive build item; a short note/commit (the cut list) or a bounded fix (under ~30 minutes) for a defect the audit found by running the code may precede it. Includes the harness requirements from the Lens (multiple processes, separate connections, one hot key, running across 60-second boundaries)
Notes that the code already uses Redis TIME so the clock-skew section is a short write-up away (an 'add' not a 'make-it-happen')
Gives time guidance relative to the ~2 hours remaining
Flags README as a WIP stub that does not yet give a clean-checkout run path
The partial file records, with evidence references, the 2-commit repo and the absence of a load test and RESULTS.md
Ends by telling the user to run a full audit before submitting
Where a runtime is available, the audit runs the limiter (or its tests) rather than only reading it, and states any defect's consequence in the brief's terms (over-admit vs over-reject)
Flags that docs/evaluator-expectations/ is tracked in the repo's history and must be removed before pushing
The partial file's Critical requirements section lists the Lens's Critical requirements with on track / at risk / not started (the load test and RESULTS.md at risk or not started)

evals.name: message-reply-against-chat-lens
evals.prompt: I'm about to send Daniel my Friday update on LinkedIn — draft is in <FIXTURES>/founder-reply/reply.md, and the Lens from our chat is in docs/evaluator-expectations. Is it good to send?
evals.expected_output: A full audit in docs/submission-audit/audit.md, verdict not-ready or fix-first. The first pass reads the reply's first sentence (a generic greeting and apology, not the result). The draft never addresses the double-charge-on-concurrent-cancellation scenario Daniel said he would test first and the user promised to handle, so that Critical requirement and the unkept promise are top gaps. It mentions Black Friday, which Daniel replaced with mid-January in his latest message. The Loom link is a placeholder. The AI disclosure says 'barely used AI, maybe 10%' while the repo notes credit Claude with most of the code, so the AI disclosure is contradicted, and the fix states the real share framed around the user's decisions and where they did not trust the AI.
expectations: Writes exactly one output file, docs/submission-audit/audit.md (no audit-final.md, gaps.md, evidence.md, inventory.md or audit-partial.md), with kind: evaluator-audit, mode, verdict and ai_disclosure in its front-matter and the numbered sections Verdict, Scorecard, Deal breakers, Requirements, Submission package, AI disclosure, Deal makers, Gaps and fixes, Notes, and the Appendix
First pass is written from the reply's first sentence and notes it opens with a greeting/apology rather than the result or the answer to Daniel's latest ask

Flags that the reply never addresses concurrent cancellations / double charging, citing Daniel's message that he will test it first and the user's own message promising to handle it, as a Critical requirement not met
Flags the Black Friday mention as built on a requirement Daniel changed in his latest message (mid-January), citing message numbers
Marks the Loom link as a placeholder / unverified package item

The AI disclosure section rates the fit as contradicted: the reply claims about 10% AI use while the repo notes credit Claude with most of the code; the fix states the real share honestly and names where the user did not trust the AI, and never suggests keeping a lower number
Cites the chat by message number (msg n) rather than by document section
Does not penalise UI polish, which Daniel said is not graded
Verdict is not-ready or fix-first, with the reason naming the unmet Critical requirement or the veto (proactive communication) being Weak

Every scorecard, trap, requirement, package and event row carries both an evidence reference into the submission (file and section or lines, commit, turn, message paragraph) or an explicit absence, and a Lens reference; every gap names the finding IDs it comes from
